title: Normalized integral and point models for the finite sf fibre
statement: Fix the finite-field datum, coefficient prime and closure, and a separated finite-type geometric base X [def-zl-classical-lisse-restriction-models; def-per-adic-base-stages]. For a finite coefficient subfield E and a raw rational sf constructible object K, define its integral PBC representative by the inverse of the fixed coefficient equivalence [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport]; bounded constructibility is preserved. The projection-normalized coefficient equivalences used by the integral completed-pullback comparison and this coefficient model coincide. For a geometric point x, compare the integral sf pullback with completed PBC pullback using the normalized comparison determined on good K-flat representatives by its finite tensor-unit generators and Roos projections [def-a1-integral-completed-pullback-interfaces; def-pod-integral-completed-comparison-data; lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison]. For a bounded constructible representative at the algebraically closed point, the normalized component is uniquely determined by these conditions, independently of any comparison witness. Normalize the sf point fibre [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] by its prescribed size-descent counit, then commute exact rationalization, degree-zero cohomology and completed point sections [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Compose this with the integral pullback comparison, extend coefficients to the closure by the actual inclusion, and apply the inverse recorded integral fibre comparison and the coefficient-equivalence unit from the normalized realization [def-zl-classical-lisse-restriction-models]. Define the integral coefficient representative, its integral, rational and common-stage counits, its normalized point-pullback comparison, and the sf point normalization to rationalized integral sections. These are the component models for the canonical comparison with the normalized realization fibre. Tensor composition is the mate of the identity-on-elements restriction-of-scalars comparison under the specified composite extension adjunction, with the site, coefficient and section universes retained. The construction uses no Weil structure and no classical local Frobenius operator.
